limits: All six verdicts rest on the verifier refusing the combined attack diff on a tamper signature (`\b_pytest\b` in the package __init__.py, planted by tamper_source_pytest_patch), as in HAR-244/256/267/283/292, so no test outcome was graded after the attacks. A clean verdict here says the 14 v1.4.0 attacks did not earn reward; it is not a graded behaviour check of those trees.

000354's task runs a custom runner; the verifier has no baseline consumer for it (verifier/baseline.log: `no baseline consumer for runner custom`), so baseline_runner is null. Its verdict rests on the refusal, so this does not change the cell.

The slice spanned two owner runs. The first HAR-298 run (Foreman worktree 20261103T205543634820Z, same commit a1ff805e1) ran every job except the final 000495 attempt and hit its 5400 s timeout while 000495 attempt 2 was running; Foreman then removed that worktree, so attempt 2's trial finished (reward 0, 14/14 executed) but mimo-census could not assemble its census row (ModuleNotFoundError). Attempts 3 and 4 of 000495 ran from the second owner run's worktree at the same commit. All jobs record repository.commit a1ff805e1 with an empty uncommitted diff.

Docker Desktop was again intermittently slow on this host. Harbor's 10 s `docker info` preflight failed for 000371 and 000390 attempt 1 before any trial existed; 000471 attempt 1 and 000495 attempts 1 and 3 wrote unscored census rows because a host-isolation daemon call at agent-environment start or the compose lock confirmation timed out before any attack ran. Each was retried as the same Docker-responsiveness preflight class, as HAR-267/292 did. Every failure is preserved under <task>/.failed-attempt<N>/ and listed in prior_attempts; census-rows.jsonl keeps every row and each verdict here is from the final attempt only. A pre-launch gate waited for two consecutive fast `docker info` calls before every attempt (docker_gate_seconds) and is excluded from wall_seconds.

wall_seconds includes docker-lock queueing: another card (HAR-299) held exclusive docker-lock slots during parts of the window, so 000371, 000390 and 000495 waited for the lock (lock_wait_seconds is the time from launch to `docker-lock: acquired slot`, which also includes uv startup). Wall times are per final attempt; every task pulled its base image cold (none cached before; each removed after). totals.wall_minutes_including_timed_prior_attempts adds the timed failed attempts.

Three other mimo base images (sha256:af20cd694d4d, sha256:2e5a71edb595, sha256:0017a76790a0) appeared on this host during the window; none is a base image of these six tasks, so they were pulled by another process and left in place.

mimo-census's own post-run process-job hook wrote process-job-error.txt in each job (`Processed report input must be outside the results home when publishing`, because the jobs dir sits under the results home); the explicit process-job publish above then succeeded for all ten trial-bearing jobs and the published copies carry processed/ reports.

Manifest verify stays unverified: the oracle and nop control cells that pending-controls.json still owes for these six rows, and fix-content cells, were not run here; a ladder cell alone cannot make a row pass. 000495 has reference_fix none in manifest.csv; the ladder does not use it.
